catalog_quote: 3.1. STRESS Stress occurs on the penultimate syllable of words up to six syllables in length. In cases when the penultimate syllable has a /ə/ vowel, the stress is shifted to the ante-penultimate syllable if such a syllable exists. Since an ante-penultimate syllable cannot exist in two syllable words, stress occurs on the penultimate syllable even though it is a /ə/. The basic patterns may be summarized as follows: (S) (S) (S) (S) 'S (S) This formula implies the following word patterns: 'S 'SS S'SS SS'SS SSS'SS SSSS'SS In words of three or more syllables with /ə/ in the penultimate syllable, according to the above stress shift rule, the following patterns occur: 'SSS S'SSS SS'SSS SSS'SSS
